description: RouteLLM benchmark prompt set — 37 prompts across the 5 task types exercised by the capability_match table (scorer.py). Distribution: 10 code, 7 reasoning, 7 summarization, 7 qa, 6 general. The runner always passes expected_task_type as task_type so ranking deterministically exercises the capability weights for that class.

prompts.prompt: Write a Python function that merges two sorted lists into one sorted list without using the built-in sort. Include type hints and a docstring.

Debug this SQL query and explain what's wrong:

SELECT u.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM users u
JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id
WHERE order_count > 5
GROUP BY u.name
ORDER BY order_count DESC;
Implement a Python class implementing a rate limiter using the token bucket algorithm. Handle concurrency with asyncio, include unit tests.
Write a TypeScript utility type that recursively makes all properties of an object readonly. Explain type variance along the way.
Write a bash one-liner that finds all files over 100MB modified in the last 30 days and prints them sorted by size, plus a cron-safe version.

Optimize this Python code for a 10M-row CSV pipeline — the current version takes 9 minutes:
csv.reader loop with dict.setdefault and per-row timedelta parsing.
Design the database schema (with SQL DDL) for a multi-tenant SaaS notes app: organizations, users, notes, sharing, and row-level security.

Implement DTO validation for this FastAPI endpoint so invalid payloads return 422 with field-level error messages:
@router.post('/devices', status_code=201)
Explain step by step why the sky is blue during the day but red/orange at sunset, starting from Rayleigh scattering and wavelength-dependent cross-sections.
Solve this logic puzzle: three boxes are labeled apples, oranges, and mixed — all labels are wrong. You may pick one fruit from one box. Which box do you pick from to relabel all three correctly?
A train leaves station A at 90 km/h; 40 minutes later a second train leaves station B, 120 km away from A, traveling toward it at 120 km/h. Where and when do they meet? Show every algebraic step.
If all bloops are razzies, all razzies are lazzies, no lazzies are fizzies, and some bloops are yellow — must some bloops not be fizzies? Prove your answer with set logic.
I flip a fair coin repeatedly until I see heads followed by tails, you flip until tails followed by heads. Do we both wait the same expected number of flips? Derive both expectations.

A farmer must ferry a wolf, a goat, and a cabbage across a river in a boat that holds the farmer plus one item. The wolf eats the goat when unattended with it; the goat eats the cabbage. Give the minimal sequence of crossings and justify minimality.
Why is it paradoxical that a country can have both a fixed minimum wage and high unemployment among unskilled workers? Walk through the classical vs. Keynesian explanations step by step.

Summarize in 5 bullet points: The modern microcontroller landscape changed dramatically in the last decade. Where designs once conflicted around proprietary vendor ecosystems, standardization around ARM cores and open toolchains pushed prices down while capability rose. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios, once power-hungry extras, became integrated on-die features. The consequence is that hobbyist boards now outperform the workstations that sent humans to the Moon by nearly every measure, and products that required dedicated engineering teams can be prototyped in a weekend. The trade-off is a widened attack surface: firmware, seldom patched in the field, now faces the same adversary profile as network-connected servers.

Summarize the following meeting transcript in three short paragraphs and list the agreed action items:

Project Atlas kickoff — Sarah opened with the quarterly targets: 30% latency reduction on the routing pipeline, zero regression on fallback coverage, and a public beta by March. Marcus pushed back on the beta date, citing unresolved pagination bugs in the analytics console. Dana committed to updating the load-test harness to simulate bursty afternoon traffic by February 10. Legal needs the provider license audit finished before any public announcement. Sarah proposed sprint reviews every two weeks instead of weekly; Marcus agreed if release notes ship with each sprint. Dana flagged that the Redis failover drill still hasn't been scheduled; Sarah will chase infrastructure and set it before the next meeting. The cost-monitoring dashboard was deprioritized in favor of the latency work.

Condense this abstract to two sentences, preserving the quantitative result: We evaluate seven large language models on a suite of 4,200 production support tickets spanning ten task categories. Routing with capability-aware selection improved first-attempt resolution by 18.4 per cent relative to a single best model, while reducing aggregate inference spend by 41 per cent under a per-token pricing model. Gains concentrated in Mixed-domain and Long-context categories where no single model dominated across subtasks.

Summarize this product review thread for a consumer electronics retailer's merchandising team:

Reviewer A: The battery lasts two days, the screen is gorgeous, but the digital assistant mishears three of five voice commands in a quiet room. Reviewer B: Identical assistant problems, resolved after the March firmware update. Reviewer C: Return window expired before the assistant degraded; customer service refused an exchange. Reviewer D: The device does everything promised and the speaker is loud enough for the kitchen. Reviewer E: Complaint about charger not being included in the box.

Give a TL;DR of the following paragraph, maximum 25 words: Distributed tracing systems generate enormous volumes of telemetry, and sampling strategy determines whether an on-call engineer sees the single failed request that caused a cascade or a statistically representative stream that hides it. Tail-based sampling retains the most interesting traces but requires buffering complete traces before deciding what to keep, trading memory for signal.

Summarize the key safety takeaways of this incident report in markdown bullets: The outage began when an autoscaling event replaced three replicas of the queue consumer during a regional storage failover. Processing lag grew past 40 minutes before alerting fired. Manual recovery drained the backlog in 22 minutes. Postmortem actions: add consumer drain-state to the health endpoint, alert on lag rather than error rate, and script the replica-rotation runbook.

Turn this long paragraph into a five-item checklist for new contributors: Releasing an SDK involves updating the changelog from the merged PR list, bumping the version in the package manifest, regenerating the migration docs snapshot, signing the artifact with the release key, and posting the announcement thread once CI has published to the registry. Each step has a companion script in the release folder; run them in order and never edit the changelog by hand after the bump.
